Elangeni School
Welcome
Welcome to Elangeni.
I hope you find this a useful site to showcase the wonderful work our pupils produce, the ethos and values we hold dear and links to other sites and resources which may be of particular interest.
Choosing the right school, for you and your child, is one of the most important decisions that you will make. Our website reflects the wide range of activities and opportunities our children engage in, especially during normal times, and our themed curriculum allows pupils to make links and recognise that skills and knowledge learnt are transferable across many aspects of life.
I am extremely proud to be the Head Teacher of Elangeni School. The pupils who attend our school will play an important role in shaping the future of our world and we, as a school, support them in identifying these skills and valuable character traits to help them succeed now and in their future both academically and as well rounded happy individuals.
‘Pupils’ SMSC development is at the heart of the school, informing curriculum planning and pastoral care, a truly whole school approach.’ – SMSC National Quality Mark auditor April 2019
CHILD PROTECTION - SAFEGUARDING STATEMENT
At Elangeni School the health, safety and well-being of every child is our prime concern. We listen to our pupils and take seriously what they tell us. Our fundamental aim is that children will enjoy their time at our school.
We want to work in partnership with parents to help our children to achieve their full potential and make a positive contribution to school life.
On rare occasions our concern about a child may mean that we have to consult other agencies even before we contact you. The procedures we follow have been laid down by the Buckinghamshire Area Child Protection Committee, and Elangeni School has adopted a Child Protection Policy in line with this for the safety of all.
Please speak to the Head teacher if you want to know more about our procedures or policy.
Click here for Child Protection Policy
If, as a parent of a pupil attending this school, you require a paper copy of the information on this website, we can provide this free of charge.

pageCache.pageTitle: Busy Living Before and After School Clubs | Elangeni School
pageCache.text:
Elangeni School
Busy Living Before School Offer - Chestnut Lane School
Busy Living is delighted to confirm that with the support of Chestnut Lane School and Governors it will be starting a new Breakfast Club based in the Dining Hall at Chestnut Lane School. The first session for the Breakfast Club will be on Thursday 4th September 2025, the start of the new autumn term, and will operate every day during term time. The Breakfast Club will be open from 07:30 and staff will accompany the Little Chestnuts Pre-school children and Chestnut Lane children to their classrooms in time for morning registration. The Elangeni children will be accompanied to the school site in readiness for going in to their classrooms from 08:35.
The club will be open to all children attending Chestnut Lane School, Little Chestnuts Preschool and Elangeni. Parents who are not already registered with Busy Living can register online now at www.busyliving.co.uk – go to the Out of School Clubs page. Bookings for the September term for both the Breakfast Club at Chestnut Lane and the After School Club at Elangeni School can be made once the current term ends.
A copy of the new Parent Handbook can be found below. This gives details of the new Breakfast Club as well as the existing After School Club, including details of charges and how the Breakfast Club will operate. The cost of the session is £10.00, to include breakfast, with a £1.00 session discount for siblings. Parents can use either or both clubs and bookings for either of the clubs can be made as frequently or infrequently as you wish! Please note, there is a £25 annual family registration fee due on first registration which is applied to the first booking.
The Breakfast Club will start at 7:30am and parents can drop off at any time from then. Access for all children attending the Breakfast Club will be down the Chestnut Lane driveway and drop off at the Fire Exit door at the rear of the Dining Hall. Please note that access is pedestrian only, you cannot drive down the school driveway. We are afraid there will be no access from the Elangeni/Woodside Avenue side as the link gate does not open until 08:00.
Children will be offered a healthy breakfast and they can choose from a variety of different foods, for instance: cereals, toast, fresh fruit, yogurt, croissants, pancakes, cheese, fruit in season, fruit juice, milk and water. Children will then have the opportunity to do arts and crafts, colouring and playing with toys and board games until it is time for school. The Chestnut Lane and Preschool children will be escorted to their classrooms by Busy Living staff and handed over to their teacher in time for registration. The Elangeni children will be accompanied to Elangeni. We very much look forward to the start of this new club and spending time with your children! Please phone or contact us via email info@busy-living.co.uk if you would like any further information at this stage. Busy Living also operates the After School Club based at Elangeni School which is next to Chestnut Lane School; children from Chestnut Lane School, although unfortunately not from Little Chestnuts Preschool, can attend. They are collected by staff at 3:05pm each day and the club runs until 6:00pm.
You can pay by credit/debit card, Tax Free Childcare or childcare vouchers received through your employer. If you are using Edenred then the reference number you need to find Busy Living is P20349540 with the postcode HP6 6AN. If using Tax Free Childcare please select the ‘childcare vouchers’ option and put your child’s unique TFC reference where it asks for the provider name/reference so your payment can be reconciled with your bookings – remember to click on the Confirm button so you bookings are saved. You can find Busy Living @ Green Ridge on the Tax Free Childcare portal under URN EY374382.
We take an optimistic view that payments paid by Tax Free Childcare or childcare vouchers will be paid within 5 days so your bookings are confirmed at the point of booking.
If you would like to check eligibility for Tax Free Childcare please visit: Tax-Free Childcare - GOV.UK (www.gov.uk)
The Busy Living office will be operating during the summer holidays to help parents with registering online if needed, or with further information. Please speak to Linda, Kevin or Alicja. Please save the Busy Living office number, 01494 702 702, which operates during from 08:00 to 18:00. Outside of these hours please email us at info@busy-living.co.uk
If you need any further help, do please call or email.
Linda, Alicja & Kevin
BLAST! Busy Living After School Team
BUSY LIVING AFTER SCHOOL TEAM (BLAST) - Elangeni School
Busy Living Ltd has been running an Ofsted registered After School at Elangeni School since July 2008 for all children aged 4-11 years and has a ‘Good’ Ofsted rating. We have the use of the Main Hall, Dining Hall and the Multi Function room for reading/homework, plus of course the various inspiring outside areas. We offer a planned, varied daily programme of craft, indoor activities and outdoor supervised sports and games which we encourage children to participate in for their health and fitness. We provide age-related activities for all children and operate an inclusive practice for children of all abilities. We collect children from the feeder school Chestnut Lane, directly from their classrooms by known, uniformed staff.
After School Club Costs & Times
We are open from 3.15pm to 6pm Monday to Friday. Bookings should be made in advance where possible to ensure availability although we are flexible and happy to take ad hoc bookings.
Fees (current from September 2025)
Annual Family Registration Fee £25 (due on new registration and annually)

We have qualified, experienced staff who work regularly at the club, so quickly become familiar with the children and their needs. We ensure new children settle in, make friends and provide an environment where they learn through play. We offer a range of activities so the children can decide what they want to do. A light bite (eg beans on toast, wraps etc) is provided at 4.30pm to keep them going until home time and water is always available.
Flexible bookings and sibling discounts are offered and make the clubs accessible for all parents, so do please ask if you require any help other than stated. We are a professional, fully insured childcare company who are Ofsted registered No EY374382 so can accept childcare vouchers or tax credits.
For more information, please e-mail/ call – we are here to help.

Elangeni School
Leave of Absence
A Request for Absence form must be submitted to Miss Burns, the Head Teacher, at least one month before the intended period of absence. Parents are strongly encouraged to speak the school before submitting the application.
Miss Burns will review each request carefully and may consider your child’s attendance record when making a decision. If permission is not granted, any absence during the requested dates will be recorded as unauthorised.
Leave of absence will not be approved immediately before or during assessment or examination periods. The school can only authorise term‑time holidays or absences in very exceptional circumstances.
Regular attendance is essential to ensure your child receives the best possible education. Any period of absence may result in your child missing important parts of their learning programme.

Elangeni School
Homework Expectations – Parent Guide
Reading – recorded in organiser
Learning Multiplication and Division facts – All Lower school and some Upper school pupils are given a book to complete their homework
English – SpaG style homework
Maths – 2/3 sections focussing on different areas
At Elangeni School, we believe that homework not only reinforces classroom learning, it also helps children to develop skills and attitudes that they need for successful lifelong learning. It should also support the development of independency, including the habits of routine, enquiry and investigation, and it should help to foster the role of parents and carers as co-educators of their children.
We believe that homework should be relevant, enjoyable and manageable. We also believe that homework facilitates the continuing development of the partnership between school and parents. Additionally, we believe that homework should not cause conflict at home between parent and child and we would always encourage parents to approach the school for support should this be the case.
If homework is handed in late or not completed, then we will notify you via SIMS Parent. Your child will stay in to complete the tasks.
Failure to complete learning three times in a half-term may result in loss of golden time on a Friday.

pageCache.pageTitle: How to become a Governor | Elangeni School
pageCache.text:
Elangeni School
Governor Vacancies
At Elangeni, we are passionate about supporting our children to help them reach their full potential. Elangeni Governing Board makes a positive contribution to children’s education by offering supportive challenge to the school’s senior leadership team to help raise standards and monitor resources. The Governing Board operates at a strategic level and is not involved in the day-to-day running of the school. The Board responsibilities include setting strategic direction of the school, monitoring progress against objectives set by Ofsted and ensuring long term financial sustainability. This is done by building a thorough knowledge of the school and its community, by both supporting and constructively challenging the school, and by ensuring accountability and compliance.
What are we looking for?
We are currently looking for new Governors with no current association with the children at the school and would be delighted to hear from anyone who has:
We welcome interest from anyone who feels they have the right experience and skills to contribute to the work of the Board.
Why become a governor?
Elangeni Governors are all volunteers who work together for the benefit of the school and are a link between the school and the community it serves. Being a Governor offers a variety of benefits:
What does the Governor role involve?
Governor role is voluntary and is not remunerated. Governors must be prepared to attend, on average, one meeting a month and also need to allow additional preparation and follow up time. Governors will receive an induction and be encouraged to engage in development opportunities, attend school events and take an interest in the wider life of the school.
The expectations of the Elangeni Governors are:
If you are interested to learn more, please contact the Chairman of the Governing Board by emailing Ms Ira Kryvorukova - ikryvorukova@elangeni.bucks.sch.uk

How to Become a Governor
National Governors Association - Be a Governor
About the role
There are over a quarter of a million volunteers governing in state schools in England. By joining them, you can make a valuable contribution to school leadership.
It is a rewarding role, working towards a shared goal of providing a high-quality education for children and young people in your community. It also provides an opportunity for personal development, building your skills and experience in areas such as project management, budgeting and working as part of a senior team.
Governing boards meet regularly to look at the big picture and the school’s long-term goals. They set the culture and values of the school, responding to opportunities and challenges. Governors and trustees work closely with the headteacher, supporting them and challenging them.
Governors typically serve at schools that are maintained by the local authority whereas trustees serve on an academy trust board. They are responsible for:
Activities can include:
Watch this video to learn more about the role
undertaking induction training and ongoing development
Who can be a governor.
There are no specific qualifications or requirements for the role - every governing board needs a balance and diversity of knowledge, skills and experience. You don't need to be a parent or to have a background in education.
To be eligible to volunteer, you need:

Apply to be a governor

You can also sign up with either of the following free recruitment services. These services work with schools to help them find volunteers.
